title: Hylo Open: Kjaersfeldt Prevails in Sensational Semifinal
article_text:
Line Kjaersfeldt dug deep to conjure a gritty win over Pornpawee Chochuwong in a intense semifinal of the HYLO Open 2026, marking a remarkable turnaround for the Dane who had fallen in the first round of her last six tournaments.

The world No.25 edged Chochuwong in a tight second game to take the match into the decider, where she trailed 15-19 but then levelled with four points in a row.

The match teetered on the edge, with Kjaersfeldt saving four match points, while Chochuwong too saved three, before the Dane converted her fourth opportunity to close it out 8-21 21-19 28-26 in 88 minutes.

“Wow, it was really intense, especially the ending. I’m just happy right now,” said Kjaersfeldt.

“I just tried to believe in the game plan and what I knew was working. I’m just happy that I kept going and kept fighting.

“The last few tournaments have been tough. Coming back from an injury, and battling a lot on finding my game. It’s working and I’m feeling better and better on court.

“Sindhu is on a good run, but I’ll try to do my best.”

In the final Kjaersfeldt takes on Pusarla V Sindhu, who had a quick path into title round beating compatriot Anmol Kharb 21-13 21-16.

It was a good day for India, with Lakshya Sen breaking a spell of below-par results to make his first final since the All England in March. Sen needed 41 minutes to get past Toma Junior Popov, 21-17 21-13.

“Controlling the net was crucial, because both of were doing well in the flat game,” said Sen. “The way I started was really good and it was important to finish in two games.”

Speaking of his challenging season, Sen said: “There were a couple of setbacks… a few niggles here and there, and I was out for a while. I wasn’t at 100 per cent, but I’m happy with the way I played here. I haven’t played these many matches at a stretch in a while. I was playing well at the All England, and I can feel I’m getting back into the rhythm again and playing good badminton.”

Sen faces Jonatan Christie, who finished earlier than he might have expected, with opponent Anders Antonsen retiring in the second game.

» Jesper Toft/Amalie Magelund edged Amri Syahnawi/Nita Violina Marwah 21-23 21-12 22-20 and take on world champions Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue.

» Christian Faust Kjaer/Rasmus Kjaer overcame Arctic Open champions Aaron Tai/Yap Roy King to earn a shot at the title against second seeds Ben Lane/Sean Vendy.

» The women’s doubles final will feature Amallia Cahaya Pratiwi/Siti Fadia Silva Ramadhanti against Hsu Yin Hui/Lin Jhih Yun.

title: Brokenhearted ex-Ryder Cup captain slams LIV Golf stars: "None showed any graciousness"
article_text:
Paul McGinley says it has broken his heart that half of the European Ryder Cup team he captained showed no graciousness towards the DP World Tour after bolting for LIV Golf.

The breakaway tour launched in June with a plethora of major champions, PGA Tour winners and ageing Ryder Cup stars.

But it remains to be seen whether the competition will return in 2027 after it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States in September.

LIV hopes to emerge from the ashes with new financiers at the helm next season following the withdrawal of Saudi Arabian funding.

But several notable players, including Sergio Garcia, Graeme McDowell and Ian Poulter, have confirmed they want no part of LIV's new era.

"I understand why they went to LIV and I think if I'd been in their position, I might have done the same," McGinley told The Times of London.

"In my view, going was not the biggest mistake.

"Their short-sightedness, in being critical of the DP World Tour as they departed, this was the problem.

"They burned their bridges as they crossed to the other side and a lot of people were offended by that.

"Half of the team I captained in the Ryder Cup at Gleneagles went to LIV. Half of them.

"Not one of them showed any graciousness to the Tour they were leaving. That broke my heart."

The aforementioned Garcia indicated earlier this week that he intends to return to the DP World Tour in 2027 in a bid to earn a place in the Ryder Cup team.

"I'm proud to call it home again," he said.

Europe's record points scorer in the biennial competition also said he is keeping his options open about returning to the PGA Tour at some point.

Some DP World Tour members, including England's Eddie Pepperell, have criticised the Spaniard and accused the former Masters champion of lacking self-awareness.

Garcia is alleged to have "flown off the handle" on the range during the 2022 BMW International Open in Germany after learning the circuit had fined him £100,000 for playing in LIV Golf's inaugural event at Centurion.

He is said to have told other golfers they should have "taken the Saudi money", adding: "You're all f---ed."

He later resigned his membership, a decision that means he will not be able to hold any leadership position in the Ryder Cup under current rules.

Garcia was also involved in a heated confrontation with a PGA Tour rules official during the 2022 Wells Fargo Championship.

After receiving an unfavourable ruling, Garcia stated he "couldn't wait" to leave the tour.

"They're now trying to be more conciliatory," added McGinley.

"'Coming back to my home' is what Sergio wrote recently, but people remember what was said four years ago.

"Back then, if these guys had been getting good advice, they would have been told, 'You've got to leave it in the right way', because LIV might be here today, gone tomorrow.

"You may want to come back to the PGA Tour or the DP World Tour, so let's do this in a classy way, expressing some appreciation as you exit. They didn't do this."

McGinley said he had seen Garcia, Poulter and Lee Westwood over the past month.

"I saw Lee down at a senior event in Chart Hills, Kent," he said.

"I spoke to him for a good hour there. I saw Ian Poulter at the Walker Cup, his son, Luke, was playing, we had a 15-minute chat.

"And I saw Sergio at the Irish Open in Doonbeg.

"I say this again, I don't criticise them for the decision they made, but feel they just didn't do it in the right way."

McGinley said there was "only one player" who he believed had handled his departure from the DP World Tour correctly.

The former Open champion, now 44, also confirmed last month that he, too, is moving on from LIV.

McGinley added: "He wrote a letter to Keith Pelley, then the CEO, that was read out to the board.

"He talked about where he came from in South Africa, the opportunities he’d been given on the European Tour, and how he was able to move on to the PGA Tour from there.

"He said he was at a point in his career where he’s getting more injuries and how this was a huge amount of money that he couldn't turn down, but that he would leave the European Tour with a heavy heart.

"I don't want this to be a hatchet job on the boys, I have relationships with them, but they made mistakes.

"We all make mistakes. Their view was so short-term.

"Their advisers needed to say, 'Hey, remember where you came from. You've been given a golden ticket at this point in your career, don't rub it in anyone's face, and don't think you can continue to play wherever you please after this."

Nations Championship: Fixtures, schedule, dates, key info as rugby's revolutionary new-look tournament gears up for finals
article_text:
It has been labelled a "tectonic shift", set to shake up the world of rugby union, but what is the Nations Championship, what have been the results so far, and what is the schedule this November?

The Nations Championship is a joint venture between Six Nations and SANZAAR that pits the giants of northern and southern hemisphere rugby against each other on a more consistent basis.

The tournament is designed to align northern and southern hemisphere rugby calendars, guaranteeing high-profile fixtures to add more structure and meaning to the existing international windows between World Cups.

The Six Nations teams - England, France, Ireland, Scotland, Wales and Italy - will take on the four Rugby Championship sides - South Africa, New Zealand, Australia, Argentina (SANZAAR) - with Fiji and Japan also representing the southern hemisphere as invited participants.

Each team will play six matches: three in July in the southern hemisphere and three in November in the northern hemisphere.

Twickenham's Allianz Stadium will then host Finals Weekend from November 27 to 29, where the inaugural champions will be crowned.

Rankings for Finals Weekend will be determined by results from the opening six matches, with each northern hemisphere team playing an additional fixture against the correspondingly ranked southern side.

title: Mitchell injury blow adds to England’s woes as Northampton sink Gloucester
article_text:
England’s injury headaches are mounting before next Sunday’s autumn opener against Australia with the scrum-half Alex Mitchell a major doubt after limping out of Northampton’s hard-fought victory over Gloucester with another hamstring problem.

It is to the credit of Northampton that they weathered that setback, withheld Gloucester’s early onslaught to score 28 unanswered points and see off the early-season pace-setters. Northampton’s last league outing here ended with 119 points scored but this was a victory founded on their defensive resilience with Tom Pearson, back in the England picture this autumn, outstanding throughout.

If Pearson’s performance will have pleased Borthwick, Mitchell’s withdrawal will not. He is already sweating on the fitness of the Northampton fly-half Fin Smith, who sat in the stands with an injured calf here, and now has concerns over his half-back partner Mitchell. England begin a crucial autumn series against the Wallabies and Borthwick now has significant concerns in two key positions. Mitchell’s injury is all the more of a worry with Archie McParland, his Northampton team-mate and fellow scrum-half, omitted from the matchday squad against Gloucester due to a calf injury sustained earlier in the week at England’s training camp.

It would be rough on Mitchell should he miss out considering it is a fourth hamstring injury of the year and his body language when leaving the field does not bode well. He suffered similar injuries during the Six Nations, at an England camp in May – recovering to take his place in the Northampton squad for the Prem final win over Exeter – and during the summer Test against Fiji. Jack van Poortvliet was England’s starting scrum-half for the summer given Mitchell’s lack of game time but when fit and firing the Northampton Saint is England’s first-choice No 9.

“Fin and Archie are both calf, Fin probably not as bad as Archie but it remains to be seen,” said Northampton’s director of rugby, Phil Dowson. “Mitchell has hurt his hamstring but I don’t know how bad. We have to be super careful with Alex and he knows his own body.”

This was always likely to be an anxious watch for Borthwick given 10 of the players on show were included in England’s mini-training camp earlier in the week. If he finds himself without both Northampton scrum-halves for the Wallabies Test, Ben Spencer would come into the frame with Harry Randall another option. Borthwick also has problems at hooker with Theo Dan going off early in Saracens’ win over Newcastle amid fitness concerns over Bath youngster Kepu Tuipulotu. Guy Pepper and Benhard van Rensburg have already been ruled out of England’s autumn campaign.

Mitchell’s withdrawal here came midway through the first half after he was caught by a Gloucester chaser when covering back to gather a loose ball. Northampton were under the pump by this stage – George Skivington’s side beginning in a manner which befitted their lofty league position.

They struck first with a well-worked move after eight minutes. Gloucester’s driving maul has been a lethal weapon this season but while Northampton withstood the drive, they had no answer to the visitors’ quick hands. The captain Seb Atkinson, who this week signed a new contract until 2029, put the excellent George Barton through a gap and he offloaded to Max Llewellyn to score. Will Joseph was next over, showing his acceleration to dash under the posts after a clever pass out the back by Atkinson, who impressed throughout. The form of those two is at least solace for Borthwick, all the more so because Atkinson has just recovered from a knee problem.

Northampton had not really got going but managed to find parity at the half-time interval. Both tries came from driving mauls, finished by Pearson and Curtis Langdon. Not exactly the type of scores for which Saints are associated but evidently their canny group of coaches had done their homework.

Midway through the second half Northampton turned down a straightforward penalty at goal to kick to the corner. It felt a risk given the scrappy nature of this contest but it ultimately paid off with George Hendy eventually splashing over on the left. With a spring in their step, Saints chalked up the bonus-point score after some nifty footwork from the replacement Rory Hutchinson to move into third in the table, sitting pretty as the league now takes a break until December.

title: Exeter 28-31 Harlequins: Visitors claim victory over Chiefs in nine-try nailbiter
article_text:
Harlequins secured back-to-back Prem victories for the first time this season, defeating Exeter Chiefs in an enthralling end-to-end contest at Sandy Park.

Quins dominated the opening exchanges, with Cadan Murley and Nick David going over before Chiefs responded through Harry Wilson's close-range effort.

Efforts from Nika Abuladze and Will Butt either side of half-time put the home side ahead but Quins fought their way back into the lead after a quick-fire brace from Lucas Schmid.

Jack Kenningham and Olly Woodburn exchanged late tries to set up a tense finish but Quins managed to scramble the ball into touch and ensure their winning run continues.

Under a bright Devon sky, it was the visitors who struck first.

Following a knock-on from the returning Manny Feyi-Waboso, Murley fed George Furbank who powered up the wing. The ball was then passed inside to Marcus Smith who fed the onrushing Murley to go over.

Quins doubled that lead soon afterwards. Attacking in the Chiefs' 22, Luke Northmore's delayed run unlocked the home defence, the centre then feeding the returning David to score despite the efforts of Woodburn.

The Chiefs, struggling to take advantage of their opportunities, finally got points on the board through Wilson, the lock driving over from a quick pick-and-go after good work from Abuladze.

Despite having a man advantage following Bryn Bradley's yellow card, the home side were repeatedly denied by aggressive Quins defending before eventually fighting their way over through Abuladze to even the scores on the verge of half-time.

After all their good defensive work in the first-half, Quins then went behind thanks to a missed tackle. Marcus Smith was unable to contain Butt in midfield, with the centre scampering up the pitch to add the Chiefs' third.

Schmid's close-range effort restored parity, with the number eight then capitalising minutes later to add another.

Following strong carrying from Sam Riley and Luke Northmore, Quins drove into the Chiefs' 22. With the ball eventually recycled wide, the back-rower drove through the final defenders to score in the corner.

Following late tries for Kenningham and Woodburn, the Chiefs found themselves only three points behind, but with the clock in the red they lost the ball at the lineout allowing Quins to kick for touch to record only their second league victory of the season.

Exeter: Haydon-Wood; Feyi-Waboso, Slade, Butt, Woodburn; Skinner, Varney; Abuladze, Yeandle (c), Iosefa-Scott; Pearson, Wilson, Roots, Vintcent, Fisilau.

Replacements: Norey, Goodrick-Clarke, Tchumbadze, Bailey, James, Wolstenholme, Hammersley, Wimbush.

Harlequins: Furbank; David, Northmore, Bradley, Murley (c); Smith, Porter; Baxter, Walker, Kerrod; Dun, Treadwell, Kenningham, Driscoll, Schmid.

Replacements: Riley, Hobson, Streeter, Williams, Browne, Evans, Friday, Isgro.

title: Huge news at Leinster suggests Jacques Nienaber is on his way back to South Africa
article_text:
Leinster are set to appoint Noel McNamara as the successor to Leo Cullen, according to a report from the Irish Times, suggesting defensive mastermind Jacques Nienaber is set for a Springboks reunion.

The report claims that McNamara, currently part of the coaching ticket at Bordeaux-Begles, will return to his former province ahead of the 2027/28 season, with Cullen set to step down at the conclusion of the current campaign in 2027.

It puts to bed rumours that former Leinster star and current Los Pumas head coach Felipe Contepomi was to take the reins, with reports that the Argentinian doctor has ruled himself out of a return to Dublin.

La Rochelle top dog Ronan O’Gara was also linked with the role, although the Corkman’s appointment in South Dublin always looked like a stretch.

The news heavily implies that Nienaber’s rumoured return to South Africa ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia is all but a done deal, as has long been speculated.

The arrival of McNamara as a head coach will almost surely copper-fasten Nienaber’s return to Rassie Erasmus’ Springboks coaching ticket, with Erasmus famous for such staff reunions. The Bok head coach has already welcomed Felix Jones after an ill-fated soujourn with Steve Borthwick’s England.

Nienaber’s current Leinster contract expires at the end of the campaign. However, a six-month break clause would allow him to potentially return to SA early, even potentially before the end of Leinster’s current campaign.

McNamara’s signing would represent a significant coup for Leinster given he only signed a contract extension with the French club earlier this year that was due to keep him at Bordeaux through to the end of the 2028/29 season.

The news suggests that Leinster and UBB have struck a deal over his early release.

The Clare native’s stock has risen considerably since leaving the Irish system several years ago.

Having previously worked in Glenstal Abbey and Clongowes, he progressed through the Leinster pathway, serving as academy manager and later taking charge of Leinster A. He also enjoyed a successful spell with Ireland U20, leading the side to a Grand Slam-winning Six Nations campaign in 2019.

Yet despite an impressive coaching CV, McNamara departed Ireland in search of fresh opportunities abroad.

A stint in New Zealand with North Harbour was followed by a move to South Africa, where he joined the Sharks coaching staff. It was there that he first crossed paths with current Bordeaux head coach Yannick Bru.

When Bru was appointed by Bordeaux in 2023, McNamara was among the key figures he recruited as part of a coaching team tasked with turning the Top 14 side into genuine contenders.

Bordeaux finished as runners-up in the Top 14 during his first two seasons at the club before finally breaking through on the European stage in 2025 with a Investec Champions Cup victory over Northampton Saints.

The French side captured back-to-back Investec Champions Cup titles after hammering Leinster this May, establishing themselves as one of the dominant forces in northern hemisphere rugby and further enhancing McNamara’s reputation as one of the game’s brightest attacking coaches.

The former Leinster academy manager had been linked with a return to Ireland earlier this year following the vacancy in Munster’s coaching staff after Roger Randle withdrew from an agreement to join the province.

Instead, McNamara opted to commit his future to Bordeaux. That decision now appears set to be short-lived.

title: Vienna Open: World number one-bound Alexander Zverev loses to Alex de Minaur in semi-finals
article_text:
Alexander Zverev lost his first match since securing the men's world number one ranking as he suffered a surprise defeat by Alex de Minaur in the semi-finals of the Vienna Open.

German top seed Zverev, who will replace Jannik Sinner at the summit of the men's rankings on Monday, lost 4-6 6-1 6-7 (4-7) to the Australian fifth seed.

Victory means 27-year-old De Minaur has leapfrogged Spain's Rafael Jodar in the race to qualify for the season-ending ATP Finals.

"I played on my terms. I was going to go out swinging and playing the right type of tennis, and that's what made the difference today."

After losing the first set, Zverev overpowered De Minaur in the second before a hard-fought decider.

With neither player able to create a break point opportunity, it was De Minaur who held his nerve in the resulting tie-break as he wrapped up victory inside two hours and 30 minutes.

De Minaur will face Spanish second seed Carlos Alcaraz in the final after he beat Daniil Medvedev in straight sets.

The seven-time Grand Slam-winner secured a 6-4 7-6 (7-2) victory over the Russian third seed to reach his fifth final of the year.

The win extended Alcaraz's unbeaten run at ATP 500 events to 25 matches with the 23-year-old last suffering defeat at that level to Holger Rune at the Barcelona Open in April 2025.

De Minaur will be competing in his fourth final of the year with his sole title coming at the Rotterdam Open in February.

title: PV Sindhu clinches Hylo Open title with straight-game win over Denmark’s Kjærfeldt
article_text:
PV Sindhu won her second title of the season, defeating Denmark’s Line Højmark Kjærfeldt 21-12, 21-14 in the final of the Hylo Open Super 500 in Germany on Sunday. The 39-minute victory earned the world No. 8 Indian 9,200 ranking points, boosting her bid for the World Tour Finals.

The victory adds to Sindhu’s Japan Open triumph in July and comes a week after she finished runner-up at the French Open.

The second-seeded Indian also collected 9,200 ranking points from the tournament, strengthening her bid to qualify for the season-ending BWF World Tour Finals.

Sindhu entered the final with a commanding 6-1 head-to-head record against the eighth-seeded Kjærfeldt.

The Dane's only previous victory over the Indian came at the 2025 Sudirman Cup Finals.

A former world champion, Sindhu maintained control throughout Sunday's contest, limiting her opponent's opportunities as she wrapped up the title in 39 minutes.

title: Bryson DeChambeau Reveals How Losing to Rory McIlroy Changed Him
article_text:
For Bryson DeChambeau, professional golf has always been about more than winning championships. The two-time U.S. Open winner built his career through intense preparation, fierce competition, and a drive to improve. Battles against the sport’s biggest names tested his game and character.

Rory McIlroy is among DeChambeau’s rivals. Their Masters and U.S. Open encounters have shaped a rivalry marked by the highs and lows of elite competition and DeChambeau’s growth as a golfer.

On entrepreneur Raj Shamani’s “Figuring Out” podcast, LIV Golf star DeChambeau reflected on his career, personal growth, and lessons from competing against golf’s best.

Bryson DeChambeau revealed that losing to Rory McIlroy at the Masters helped shape him into a better person. He explained that difficult moments are necessary for personal growth, even when they’re frustrating.

“I think this is a good little point, too. It’s not that I like being humbled; I like having that perspective, right? It sucks getting humbled. Everybody doesn’t like it, but it needs to happen,” DeChambeau said.

The American said humility is key to personal growth, then reflected on his rivalry with McIlroy and their contrasting results at two majors.

“Whether it’s me losing the Masters to Rory or him losing to me at the U.S. Open when I won, it’s so good for us,” DeChambeau explained.

McIlroy defeated DeChambeau at the 2025 Masters, while DeChambeau beat the Northern Irishman during their final-round battle at the 2024 U.S. Open at Pinehurst No. 2.

DeChambeau said golf can humble even the best; players may feel at their peak one day, then struggle to hit a shot the next.

“And I think that’s what’s so beautiful about it. That difficult moment is honestly what has helped shape me into a better person today. So, if I didn’t have that, I wouldn’t be the person I am today,” he added.

DeChambeau sees competition as more than golf, and for him wins and setbacks offer perspective and foster personal growth.

Alongside his personal reflections, DeChambeau also discussed his commitment to LIV Golf and its proposed restructuring. The Crushers GC captain said he remains particularly interested in the league’s team-based format.

Speaking about LIV’s original management, he acknowledged that the parent company was not managed effectively. However, he argued that the teams themselves were generating revenue.

DeChambeau said Crushers GC brought in nearly $29 million in revenue last year and had $21 million in costs, including player payments, travel, and operations, leaving about $8 million in EBITDA.

“The teams were doing well, but then all the player payments and everything got pushed down to the teams when they went bankrupt because the top company wasn’t being run effectively,” he said.

After Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund said it would end funding after the 2026 season, LIV entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy. A restructuring deal involving BC Partners offered a possible path forward.

DeChambeau believes the next version of LIV can operate more effectively. He said the proposed business model makes sense and hoped the league could continue long term.

“It’s no funny business, no nothing. It’s going to be done right. And this is going to be a league, hopefully, that exists forever,” he said.

He explained that players previously received large upfront payments due to limited governance and control; the new model could offer greater ownership and influence instead.

“This time around, it’s more the opposite. We’re not really getting paid, but we do have the governance, you know, control,” DeChambeau explained.

His support for LIV centers on its team format and players’ potential role in shaping its future. Whether restructuring ensures long-term financial stability remains unclear.

title: Brooks Koepka may have now answered one of the key questions Bryson DeChambeau had about his future
article_text:
Brooks Koepka could not resist a dig at Bryson DeChambeau during an interview this week, with the five-time major champion making fun of his old rival’s comments about Rory McIlroy from the 2025 Masters.

Koepka and DeChambeau have had their issues over a number of years. It was clear that the two men were not particularly fond of each other, though they were eventually able to put those problems to one side ahead of the 2021 Ryder Cup at Whistling Straits.

They also seemed to get along much better once they both moved to LIV Golf. However, Koepka went on to become the first big name to walk away from the league in late 2025.

And it would appear that Koepka has made little attempt to stay in touch with DeChambeau now that he has moved back to the PGA Tour.

Speaking to Dan Rapaport in an interview posted this week, Koepka joked that he can understand why no-one would want to speak to DeChambeau, when asked about the LIV star highlighting that Rory McIlroy did not talk to him during the final round of The Masters last year.

Of course, McIlroy himself made his feelings about DeChambeau known at The Open Championship this year, with the Northern Irishman admitting he is not a fan of the two-time US Open champion.

Do you think Jackson Koivun is more likely to win his first major than Brooks Koepka is to win his sixth next year? 🤔

The digs from the likes of Koepka and McIlroy perhaps highlight one of the reasons DeChambeau looks set to stay with LIV Golf beyond this year given what he previously said about a PGA Tour return.

In an interview with Skratch in May, DeChambeau noted that he would only be interested in coming back to the PGA Tour if the membership wanted him back.

Koepka and McIlroy do not speak for the rest of the players, obviously. However, they are extremely influential. No active player on the PGA Tour can compete with the pair for major victories, so their comments are significant.

DeChambeau has become accustomed to being the superstar of his league. On LIV, he was the biggest name. He was the player that many fans came to see. And the other players seemed to be very happy to protect him when he would face any criticism or ridicule from the outside.

He would clearly have plenty of friends if he returned to the PGA Tour. DeChambeau was praised whenever his teammates had an opportunity to talk about him during the 2025 Ryder Cup at Bethpage.

However, DeChambeau is loved and idolised on LIV. He is obviously aware that he would be considered a much more divisive character if he returned to the PGA Tour, and does not have the desire to take on that particular challenge.

title: Wales centre Hawkins determined to make World Cup
article_text:
Wales centre Joe Hawkins says missing the previous World Cup has made him more determined to make the next global tournament in Australia in 12 months.

Following his move from Ospreys to Exeter in 2023, Hawkins was deemed ineligible to play for Wales by Welsh rugby's Professional Rugby Board (PRB) because of the 25-cap rule.

The rule says players who have fewer than 25 caps are unavailable to play for Wales if they are not involved with a Welsh club.

This ruled him out of the 2023 World Cup in France but Hawkins has since returned to the national side after signing for Scarlets.

"I have no regrets," said 24-year-old Hawkins.

"It would have been nice to have a World Cup under my belt already, but that just makes me even more excited for potentially what's ahead over the next year.

"I loved my couple of years in Exeter with the life experience and playing in the Prem, where you can see a lot of the boys are thriving in now."

Wales have a minimum of 12 matches before the World Cup, starting with the Nations Championship opener against Japan in Cardiff next Saturday.

"It's always in the back of your mind, knowing you're going into a World Cup year," said Hawkins.

"You can probably see from performances from other boys in all positions in the squads that in a World Cup year, the intensity probably rises at the clubs.

"Boys are playing for positions and knowing that's the carrot at the end of the year.

"But if you're not taking care of the here and now you're not going to get that far."

Hawkins, 24, and Scarlets partner Eddie James have developed as Wales' first-choice centre pairing during the past 12 months.

Wales head coach Steve Tandy has selected five different starting midfield partnerships in 13 games since taking charge in September 2025.

Hawkins and James are the most prolific pair, having been together for seven games which include victory in an uncapped match against Barbarians.

Tandy did go back to Ben Thomas and Max Llewellyn for the 43-0 defeat by South Africa in July, but the Scarlets pair have been the preferred option.

"Eddie and I have a good relationship on and off the field," said Hawkins.

"That is starting to grow on the pitch with the more opportunities we get together."

The make-up of the Wales midfield has caused debate with Tandy and attack coach Matt Sherratt wanting a creative ball-playing inside centre like Hawkins or Thomas.

This leaves James as the physical presence at outside centre with Tandy stating he sees the Carmarthen-born 24-year-old's long-term future as a Test 13.

Many observers believe James should be considered as a 12 but Wales are determined to keep their creative options open.

With Thomas missing because of a calf injury, Hawkins appears to be competing for the Wales' 12 jersey with uncapped Dragons centre Aneurin Owen, although Llewellyn has also featured at inside centre for Gloucester this season.

"The ball-playing stuff is stuff I enjoy doing but you still need to go forward as well and I feel like I can also produce that side of it," said Hawkins.

"Matt [Sherratt] likes you always in and around that first receiver position so you are always in those decision-making roles.

"You've got to be comfortable on the ball and making decisions at high speed.

"But there's not always going to be opportunities to ball play, so you've got to try and have a bit of a rounded game."

Hawkins has also been employed as an outside-half by Scarlets but he sees his future at 12.

"It gives me a lot more respect for the 10s, having been in there, with all the work they do," he added.

"It probably helps me when I play centre from being a 10, I know what they need from me a little bit more, so the information and communication I'm feeding helps the whole team."

title: Edinburgh lose unbeaten URC record at hands of Benetton
article_text:
Edinburgh's unbeaten start to this season's URC came to an end as they lost 31-12 to Benetton in Italy.

Sean Everitt's side had won their opening four matches of the campaign but were behind inside two minutes in this one when Piero Gritti crossed for the previously winless Italians.

Benetton were the better side in the opening quarter, and their momentum was not significantly checked, even when when Matias Medrano's hit on Grant Gilchrist earned him a 20-minute red card.

Ignacio Mendy went over for a second try before Callum Hunter-Hill's yellow card left Edinburgh with 14 men.

Bautista Bernasconi's try, plus Jacob Umaga's penalty, gave Benetton an 18-0 interval lead - an advantage that was stretched further after the break by another Umaga penalty and Onisi Ratave's try.

Harri Morris and Harry Paterson both went over for Edinburgh to add an air of respectability to the scoreline, but a late penalty ensured the hosts had the final word.

title: 'Really proud': Unbeaten Glasgow Warriors enjoying view from URC summit
article_text:
There are new leaders in the URC in the shape of Glasgow Warriors who are now the only unbeaten team in the competition.

They went top on Friday night by claiming a 29-20 bonus point win over the 10Bet Lions at Scotstoun and stayed there with previous frontrunners Edinburgh Rugby going down to their first defeat of the season at the hands of Benetton Rugby.

For the second round in a row, Glasgow left it late.

Last weekend, they snatched victory away to Benetton with a 78th minute try. This time, the decisive touchdown came in the 76th minute.

Full-back Ollie Smith was the man to cross with George Horne then landing two shots at goal to seal the win and deny the Lions a losing bonus point.

Scotland squad scrum-half Horne said: “We came out pretty hot in the first half. Then, in the second half, they held on to the ball and put us under pressure.

“We killed ourselves, giving away too many penalties and they ended up scoring. All the momentum was against us.

“But the main thing is we came back in. The scrum dug us out at the end and we are just buzzing to get the five points.

“I am really proud of the boys. The experienced guys stepped up to bring us over the line.”

Head coach Franco Smith commented: “I expected it to be a fight from the start. The Lions rolled out a classy outfit. I don’t think they were missing many people. So I wasn’t surprised with the effort from them.”

Smith was without 11 of the 19 Glasgow players selected for Scotland’s Nations Championship campaign, making the victory over a strong Lions side all the more creditable.

“I’m proud of everybody who contributes to prepare the boys for these important games when we are depleted,” he said.

“To see a result is really important and compliments the rugby programme. I’m really proud that the players applied themselves so well.”

Meanwhile, fellow Scottish side Edinburgh saw their dream start to the league campaign come to an abrupt end as they were beaten 31-12 by Benetton in Treviso.

It was a first win of the season for the Italian hosts much to the delight of their Kiwi head coach Wayne Pivac.

“I am just so pleased for the group because we have come so close in every other game,” said the former Wales boss.

“So to get it across the line was pretty special.

“It’s just so good to get that monkey off the back, that first win.

“It’s huge for the group. I am very happy for the players because they have put in so much hard work.”

With Edinburgh dropping down to fifth, it’s now three South African sides immediately below Glasgow in the table – the Vodacom Bulls, the DHL Stormers and the Hollywoodbets Sharks.

title: Jerome Kaino joins Springboks' pool rivals ahead of 2027 Rugby World Cup
article_text:
Georgia have bolstered their coaching ranks ahead of the upcoming Rugby World Cup in 2027 with the appointment of former All Blacks great Jerome Kaino.

The Lelos will share Pool B with South Africa, Italy and Romania in a little under one year’s time.

The two-time Rugby World Cup winner has joined the Lelos coaching staff for the November international window, where he will work as an assistant coach under Pierre-Henri Broncan.

Kaino’s brief will focus on contact areas and attacking rucks as Georgia continue their preparations for a month that includes Tests against Canada, Tonga and the USA.

The appointment reunites Kaino with Broncan, with the pair having previously worked together at French heavyweights Toulouse.

Despite linking up with the Georgian national side, the 43-year-old will retain his existing role at Toulouse.

Georgia confirmed the appointment in a statement, describing Kaino as a specialist addition to Broncan’s backroom team for the November programme.

Born in American Samoa in 1983, Kaino moved to New Zealand with his family at the age of four and would go on to establish himself as one of the outstanding back-row forwards of his generation.

After developing through the Auckland system, he represented both Auckland and the Blues between 2004 and 2018, becoming a mainstay of New Zealand rugby during one of the most successful periods in the nation’s history.

His rise first gathered pace in 2004 when he helped the Junior All Blacks win the World Rugby Under-21 Championship and was subsequently named the world’s Under-21 Player of the Year.

That same year brought his senior All Blacks debut. He went to win 81 Test caps, two Rugby World Cup triumphs in 2011 and 2015, and five Rugby Championship titles.

The 6’5, 113kg Kaino was named New Zealand Player of the Year in 2011 after playing a pivotal role in the All Blacks ending their 24-year wait for a World Cup on home soil.

Following the conclusion of his Super Rugby career, Kaino moved to France where he spent the final three seasons of his playing career with Toulouse. The powerhouse loose forward lifted the Top 14 title in both 2019 and 2021, while also helping Toulouse capture the Champions Cup in what proved to be the final season of his playing career.

Kaino immediately transitioned into coaching and has spent the past five years with Toulouse working in skills development and with the club’s Under-21 programme.

title: ‘Not an accident’: The qualities behind Fraser McReight’s historic award win
article_text:
When Les Kiss first met Fraser McReight, the qualities that would make the Queensland Reds and Wallabies flanker a future John Eales Medallist were already clear to see. “It’s not an accident where he’s got to,” Kiss said this week, after McReight made history.

McReight received two awards at the 2026 Rugby Australia Awards, capping off a career-best 12 months in gold. The openside became the first Queensland player in 20 years to be named a John Eales Medallist, which is awarded to the Wallabies’ players’ player.

Eales himself presented the prestigious award to McReight, who was celebrated with a deafening cheer of support from the Wallabies and others in attendance. But after walking off the stage and down some steps, McReight declared,“I can get a lot better.”

It’s that constant thirst for improvement that led McReight to that moment, as Kiss explained the next morning. The two spent a few Super Rugby Pacific campaigns together at the Reds, with Kiss bestowing captaincy duties upon McReight ahead of the 2026 season.

“From the first day I met Fraser, there’s a deep drive in him, a deep drive to just become so good at his craft. He’s a hard marker on himself, definitely, but that deep drive is essential for that position. When I first met him, I could see why he’s the type of player he is,” Kiss said.

“My growth with him, when he became a leader or a captain, he has a great sense of understanding. The nature of that position, it’s so dialled in – in a way it’s a selfish pursuit isn’t it? Selfish but he’s an unbelievable team man and he knows how to bring people together with him.

“He has that capacity so say, my world is this, whatever you guys think I’m just going to try and win this world. But at the same time, his sense of being able to be relatable right across the team, build culture… his qualities are fantastic.

“Craft is great because he’s driven, he practises it. Has great leadership qualities and has a wonderful team-first approach to the whole thing.”

McReight set the tone during last year’s Spring Tour by winning five turnovers and making a team-high number of tackles against England. The backrower maintained that high-level throughout Super Rugby Pacific and another 10 Test appearances since then.

Jeremy Paul, Rob Valetini and Dave Rennie have all spoken highly of McReight in recent years, with the Queenslander forging his own legacy in the golden number seven jersey – which was worn for many years by four-time John Eales Medal winner Michael Hooper.

McReight produced a stunning performance against Six Nations giants France in July, winning two turnovers, scoring a couple of tries, and making 17 tackles. The Wallaby’s try-saving efforts were celebrated at the RA Awards too, taking home Defender of the Year.

“It’s the nature of the beast because that’s what it is, it’s the nature of the beast that you’re never quite satisfied,” Kiss told reporters.

“And his pursuit of being greater, you see it every day, that’s for sure.

“That quality is essential for someone like him but I think that’s something that’s throughout the whole group to tell you the truth. Becoming more self-aware about how much more is in them in a whole and he’s an individual that epitomises that wonderfully on a daily basis.

“It’s not an accident where he’s got to. He’s got a talent, he works on the craft around it, he’s driven and he just wants to be better every day.”

title: WTA Rankings: Alex Eala and Leylah Fernandez missed opportunity, Diana Shnaider nears top 10, Harriet Dart +32
article_text:
Harriet Dart and Diana Shnaider were this week’s big winners as they lifted the titles in Guangzhou and Tokyo, respectively.

Dart, who came through qualifying, lifted the first WTA Tour title of her career as she came from a set down to beat Austrian teenager Lilli Tagger in the Guangzhou Open final on Sunday.

The 30-year-old spurned two match points at 5-3 up in the decider but eventually closed out the win in a 4-6, 6-3, 6-4 triumph against the 18-year-old at the WTA 250 event.

In her semi-final victory over 16-year-old Sun Xinran, the tears flowed from the Brit but in her ceremony speech, Dart kept her calm and paid tribute to Tagger and her team.

She said on court, “I will try and not get too emotional. Firstly, Lilli, you are so young, and you have a huge career ahead of you. Congratulations on an amazing week and year. I have no doubt you will win so many more titles, so well done to you and your team for all of your hard work.”

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Dart added, “A big thank you to my team with me this week. My boyfriend Steven, my fitness coach Dario but also the people at home, my coach Marion [Bartolli], really appreciate all your hard work. But also my family, my parents, and my sister Phoebe. I love you guys and thank you for always being there for me and supporting me every step of the way.”

Dart started this week ranked 115th in the world but she has shot up 32 places to 83rd in the live rankings – 13 spots off her career best. Conversely, the young Austrian, who was seeking her second WTA Tour title, is 53rd in the rankings.

The other big rankings risers in the top 100 include 20-year-old Kaitlin Quevedo, who lost in the semi-finals in Guangzhou but jumped up 16 spots to 70th in a personal best milestone.

Moreover, Kamilla Rakhimova catapulted herself up 22 places to a career-high of 44 but Janice Tjen has fallen 28 positions to 75 as her points from last year’s Chennai Open title have dropped off.

Further up the rankings, Shnaider’s WTA 500 win at the Pan Pacific Open sees her equal her best-ever ranking of 11 after beating Leylah Fernandez in three sets in the final on Sunday.

The Russian, who climbs two spots for her efforts this week at the WTA 500 tournament, beat the Canadian 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 victory and is now just under 700 points behind 10th-ranked Marta Kostyuk.

For Fernandez, this was a missed opportunity to leapfrog many of her rivals into 16th but as a result of finishing the runner-up in Tokyo, she is on 2,201 points in 19th.

Incidentally, Alex Eala stays in 18th but if she had beaten Shnaider in her quarter-final, where she was two points from victory, the 21-year-old would have jumped to a career-high of 16.

The Filipina will hope to end the year with her best-ever ranking when she begins her Hong Kong Open campaign this week, where 250 WTA points are up for grabs.

There has been no change at all in the rankings in regards to the top 10 as they prepare for the WTA Finals, which gets underway on 8 November in Indian Wells.

Former world No 9 Victoria Mboko, who is still out with a knee injury, has dropped six spots to 21st in the big casualty in the top of the rankings.

title: Europe guaranteed two titles, Kjaærsfeldt stuns Chochuwong
article_text:
Line Kjaersfeldt came through a 28-26 decider against the top seed to reach the women’s singles final, while all-European finals in men’s and mixed doubles guarantee two European champions at the HYLO Open 2026.

Line Kjaersfeldt produced the comeback of the day in the women’s singles semifinals. The Danish eighth seed lost the opening game 8-21 to top seed Pornpawee Chochuwong of Thailand. She levelled at 21-19, then held her nerve through an extended decider to win 28-26.

“I’m really happy and really relieved. It was a tough match today and very intense,” said Kjaersfeldt. “I had a really bad start, but I worked myself in there.”

She will meet P.V. Sindhu in the final, after the Indian second seed defeated compatriot Anmol Kharb in two games.

Europe will be crowned in mixed doubles. Unseeded Danes Jesper Toft/Amalie Cecilie Kudsk recovered from losing the first game to defeat Indonesian fifth seeds Amri Syahnawi/Nita Violina Marwah 21-23, 21-12, 22-20. They face French second seeds Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue, who came through a three-game battle with Malaysia’s Hoo Pang Ron/Lai Pei Jing 22-20, 16-21, 21-17.

The men’s doubles final will also be all-European. English second seeds Ben Lane/Sean Vendy defeated France’s Julien Maio/William Villeger in a tense semifinal. They will meet Denmark’s Christian Faust Kjær/Rasmus Kjær, who defeated Malaysia’s Aaron Tai/Yap Roy King.

There was disappointment in the men’s singles. Top seed Anders Antonsen retired from his semifinal against Indonesia’s Jonatan Christie while being behind 18-21, 13-16.  France’s Toma Junior Popov also bowed out, losing 17-21 13-21 to India’s Lakshya Sen, who meets Christie in the final.

In women’s doubles, Bulgaria’s Gabriela Stoeva/Stefani Stoeva pushed Indonesian fifth seeds Amallia Cahaya Pratiwi/Siti Fadia Silva Ramadhanti all the way in the second game but lost 16-21 22-24.

The finals begin at 2pm (CET) on Sunday 1 November at the Saarlandhalle.

title: One League, Two Sponsorship Rulebooks
article_text:
Lazio’s Polymarket shirt deal didn’t survive the summer. In August, the Rome club parted with the prediction-market company after Italian regulators blocked its website. Yet Serie A had signed its own Polymarket agreement only months earlier, and that partnership was aimed squarely at the United States.

The same company could be ruled out on a Lazio shirt in Italy while appearing in the league’s American media. The difference lies in where each deal is meant to operate.

Lazio agreed a two-season sponsorship with Polymarket in April 2026, reportedly worth around €19 million, with an option for another year. It was a significant deal for a club that had struggled to fill the front of its shirt.

A March breakdown of Serie A shirt sponsorship earnings identified Lazio as the only club in the division without a main shirt partner. Inter and Milan, by comparison, were each receiving around €30 million annually from their respective arrangements.

By July, the optimism had faded. Italy’s Customs and Monopolies Agency, known as ADM, had again blocked access to the platform, treating it as an unauthorised gambling operator. Keeping its branding on Lazio shirts had become difficult to reconcile with the Italian advertising rules.

Italy’s Dignity Decree restricts advertising for gambling and betting with cash winnings, including sports sponsorship. Whether a prediction market belongs in that category has been central to the Polymarket dispute. The company’s description of its product as a prediction exchange didn’t prevent ADM from treating its Italian activities as unauthorised gambling.

The United States has a separate regulatory system, and access to prediction markets can depend on the state and the product offered. Readers can see how these distinctions work in practice at CBS Sports Polymarket review, which outlines US eligibility requirements, location restrictions and promotional terms. Those conditions explain who may use the American platform, not whether Polymarket’s branding is permitted on a Serie A shirt in Italy.

Italian clubs need more than assurances about a sponsor’s US operations. They also need to know whether the branding they sell is permitted at home.

On 14 May 2026, Serie A USA named Polymarket its exclusive prediction-market partner in the United States under a multi-year arrangement. According to the league’s official announcement, the agreement covers US media and digital branding, alongside prediction markets using official Serie A data supplied through Genius Sports.

Those are quite different commercial rights from putting a company logo on a Lazio shirt worn in Italian domestic competition. The league’s deal was expressly regional, aimed at American supporters rather than Italian customers.

- 14 May: Serie A USA announced its American partnership with Polymarket.

- July: Italian restrictions again put Lazio’s shirt deal in doubt.

- 11 August: Lazio and Polymarket agreed to end their sponsorship.

Lazio’s announcement concerned the club’s contract. It didn’t say that Serie A USA’s separate agreement had been cancelled.

There was an important financial detail in the 11 August settlement. Lazio said Polymarket would pay the full amount stipulated for the 2026/27 season, even though the sponsorship was ending early. Reports valued that season’s portion at approximately €9.5 million.

That protects one season’s fee, but the shirt space still needs a new buyer for future campaigns. The club and Polymarket also left open the possibility of working together again if the regulatory position changes.

Serie A clubs are looking beyond Italy for new commercial income, particularly in the American market. Regional media partnerships allow the league to reach that audience without necessarily placing the same branding in Italian stadiums.

Lazio’s experience shows why those distinctions need to be written into agreements from the outset. A sponsor can have an international profile and still encounter a local restriction serious enough to end a shirt deal. The league may continue to pursue US partnerships, but clubs selling sponsorship space in Italy have to account for the rules governing that space.

title: Valentin Vacherot Creates Monaco History, Stuns Taylor Fritz To Reach Basel Final
article_text:
Valentin Vacherot created Monegasque tennis history by stunning sixth seed Taylor Fritz in straight sets to reach the Swiss Indoors Basel final.

Monegasque tennis star Valentin Vacherot on Saturday, October 31, became the first from his country to qualify for the final of the Swiss Indoors, after he stunned sixth seed Taylor Fritz in straight sets in the semifinal.

This is Vacherot’s biggest win since he beat Alex de Minaur in the quarterfinals of the Monte-Carlo Masters.

Vacherot booked his place in his first final of the season with a 7-6(5), 6-3 win against Fritz at the ATP 500 event, becoming the first player from Monaco to reach the tournament’s championship match.

Vacherot matched Fritz’s powerful serve with a brilliant serving display of his own and held his nerve in the key moments to seal his place in the final.

Vacherot fought back from a 1-4 deficit in the first-set tie-break, winning six of the next seven points to take the opener. He then bagged a decisive break at 4-3 in the second set to clinch the win in one hour and 26 minutes.

“You just have to pray on the returns because Taylor is one of the best servers on Tour. His spots are just amazing. Sometimes you can anticipate it, but you can’t even touch it," Vacherot said after the match.

“I am just super happy I got that break at 4-3 in the second set. I guessed well and executed it well," Vacherot added.

The victory brought him level at 1-1 in his Lexus ATP Head2Head rivalry with Fritz, avenging his first-round loss to the American at the same tournament last year.

Having reached his first final of the year and his maiden ATP 500 championship match, Vacherot is now chasing his first title since his brilliant win at the 2025 Rolex Shanghai Masters.

Vacherot’s fairytale run at the Masters 1000 event saw him become the lowest-ranked champion in the series’ history since its inception in 1990.

Vacherot will next face either eighth seed Jiri Lehecka or Jan-Lennard Struff in the Basel final.

title: Shnaider survives Fernandez fightback to win sixth career crown in Tokyo
article_text:
No. 3 seed Diana Shnaider appeared to be cruising toward her first title of the season after building a 6-4, 4-0 lead against Leylah Fernandez in the Toray Pan Pacific Open final in Tokyo on Sunday.

But that's when things got complicated for the 22-year-old. Fernandez mounted a spirited comeback, winning seven of the next eight games to take the second set 7-5 and force a decider.

Fernandez carried that momentum into the third set, holding serve before earning three break points on Shnaider's serve. However, Shnaider saved all three to level the set at 1-1. After the players exchanged holds, Shnaider broke serve in the fifth game and won the next three games to close out a 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 victory in 2 hours, 18 minutes.

The victory marks Shnaider's first title of the season and the sixth of her career.

SUPER SHNAIDER 🏆 Diana Shnaider defeats Fernandez 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 in Tokyo to claim her sixth career singles title! #torayppo https://t.co/1RaHGHbUFV

Shnaider, who had lost all four semifinals she reached this year, has now won six consecutive finals on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz. Her only defeat in a WTA final came in her first career championship match at the 2023 Ningbo Open, where she lost to Ons Jabeur. Four of her six titles have now come on hard courts, including her third WTA 500 crown in Tokyo today.

"Firstly, I would like to congratulate Leylah on an amazing week, last week, some great achievements through this Asia Swing," Shnaider said during the on-court presentation ceremony. "Congrats to you, your coach, your family back home. Keep going and for sure hope to see you more in the finals like this in the future.

"I also want to say thanks to and congratulate my coach who is here with me to achieving our first title this season. It means definitely a lot, so definitely a great achievement and a great finish to the season. I want to also say huge thanks to my family who is watching at home and also super happy."

The victory is projected to lift Shnaider back to a career-high No. 11 in the WTA PIF Rankings.

After losing her first two meetings with Fernandez, Shnaider has now won their last four encounters. This was her third victory over the Canadian this season, following wins in Adelaide on hard courts and Charleston on clay.

For Fernandez, the defeat was only her fifth in her last 21 matches. That stretch includes her sixth career title in Singapore and a runner-up finish in Ningbo last week.

title: PV Sindhu, Lakshya enter finals at Hylo Open

last week. The two-time Olympic medallist defeated 19-year-old Anmol 21-13, 21-16 in just 32 minutes in Saarbrucken, Germany. Sindhu will play eighth-seeded Dane Line Hojmark Kjaersfeldt, who stunned top seed Pornpawee Chochuwong 8-21, 21-19, 28-26, in the final.

also made it to the final with a 21-17, 21-13 victory against Toma Junior Popov of France. Lakshya, who is working hard to get back to his best, will face the winner of the semifinal between Anders Antonsen of Denmark and Jonatan Christie of Indonesia.

Anmol made a promising start, troubling Sindhu with accurate smashes and deep shots in the first game. However, the veteran gradually settled into her rhythm and began dictating the rallies. Despite a brief fightback from the youngster, Sindhu entered the interval with an 11-9 lead. Sindhu raised the tempo after the break and earned seven game points before comfortably closing out the first game.

Anmol stepped up her aggression after the break in the second game and even managed to establish a 15-13 lead with two successive smashes. However, a couple of unforced errors allowed Sindhu to draw level at 15-15. Sensing an opportunity, Sindhu produced a cleverly disguised drop shot to move ahead 17-15.

With Anmol's errors mounting, Sindhu maintained her composure to earn four match points and converted the first.

Jonatan Christie is usually a very aggressive player who loves to smash the shuttlecock whenever the opportunity arises.

title: Carlos Alcaraz and Alex De Minaur ranking points and prize money after Vienna Open final
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz brushed aside Alex De Minaur to win the Vienna Open title for the first time in his career.

Alcaraz had a perfect 6-0 record against the Australian heading into the contest but after De Minaur’s three-set win over new No 1 Alexander Zverev in the semi-finals, many thought a close battle was in store.

And while the 27-year-old had multiple game points in a number of games in the first set, he still ended up losing it 6-1 in 37 minutes as the Spaniard put in a ruthless display.

De Minaur hit 79% of his first serves in but ended up winning just 48% of those deliveries, as the world No 3 outclassed his opponent on Sunday afternoon.

Alcaraz, who missed more than four months of the season due to a wrist injury, had to work harder for his spoils in the second set but still was comfortable enough in a 6-1, 6-4 victory in one hour, 28 minutes.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Alcaraz claimed his fourth title of 2026 and the 28th of his glittering career, while De Minaur, who lost his third title match in a row this year, fell to 11-12 in ATP Tour finals.

While the Aussie would dearly have loved to have won in Vienna and beaten Alcaraz for the first time, he is up to eighth in the rankings on 3,210 points.

More importantly, though, the former world No 5 has leapfrogged his rivals into ninth in the ATP Finals Race, which is the last qualification spot for the season-ending event in Turin.

His final run puts him on 3,210 points, just one solitary point ahead of Rafael Jodar in 10th. Meanwhile, Alcaraz is third in the Race on 5,100 points and is up to 6,100 points in the live rankings.

That still puts him 3,350 points behind Jannik Sinner, who is just 100 points back from Zverev. Alcaraz can close that gap significantly, however, with a strong end to the season.

He pockets 500 ranking points and £437,718 in prize money, while De Minaur collects 330 ranking points and £235,494 in earnings. Both will hope to add to both of these tallies when the Paris Masters gets underway this coming week.

This ATP Finals Race is set to go down to the wire, with De Minaur, Rafael Jodar, Novak Djokovic and Taylor Fritz, among others, all in with a shot at qualifying after world No 2 Sinner ended his season early due to a knee injury.

title: Rafael Jodar makes ATP Rankings history as he secures huge milestone in standout season
article_text:
Rafael Jodar will make history next week after the Spaniard secured his debut inside the top 10 of the ATP Rankings.

The third seed at the Swiss Indoors in Basel this week, Jodar was beaten by Valentin Vacherot in the second round of the ATP 500 event.

However, with Vacherot going on to defeat Taylor Fritz in the semi-final of the event on Saturday, 20-year-old Jodar is now guaranteed to reach the top 10 of the ATP Rankings for the first time next week.

Currently ranked 11th in the world, the Spaniard is projected to rise one place to world No 10 — and will achieve something that no man in the history of the men’s game can match.

Jodar will become the first player since the ATP Rankings were introduced in 1973 to reach the top 10 during his first full season on tour, having only made his Grand Slam debut at the Australian Open in January, and his Masters 1000 debut at the Indian Wells Open in March.

The Spaniard will also become the player with the second shortest gap between his top 100 debut and his top 10 debut, with the 217 days between those two milestones only bettered by the 210 days between Boris Becker’s top 100 and top 10 debuts back in 1985.

Just 287 days separate the start of Jodar’s first full season and his top 10 debut, cementing a remarkable rise for the Spaniard who has become one of the most talked-about players in men’s tennis.

Jodar’s breakout season has been full of notable milestones, perhaps none more so than winning his first ATP Tour title at the Grand Prix Hassan II in Marrakesh this May.

The Spaniard defeated Marco Trungelliti to lift the first tour-level title of his career, a result that was followed by two more runner-up finishes at ATP level.

Jodar reached the first ATP 500 final of his career at the Citi Open in July, falling to Taylor Fritz in the championship match, while he reached the first Masters 1000 final of his career at the Shanghai Masters in October — falling in three tight sets to compatriot Alejandro Davidovich Fokina.

At Masters 1000 level, the Spaniard was also a semi-finalist on his tournament debut at the Canadian Open in August, while he was also a quarter-finalist at both the Madrid Open and Italian Open during the spring.

And, he also reached his first Grand Slam quarter-final in just his second major main draw appearance at Roland Garros.

Seeded 27th in Paris, it took second seed and eventual champion Alexander Zverev to stop him in the last eight, with Jodar also reaching the third round of Wimbledon just a few weeks later.

Following on from his second-round showing in Basel, Jodar will return to action at the Paris Masters next week.

The Spaniard is the ninth seed at the Masters 1000 tournament and will start his campaign in round one against Alejandro Tabilo, with a potential clash versus fifth seed Flavio Cobolli in the third round.

Jodar is among those battling for a place in the ATP Finals, with the 20-year-old knocked down to 10th place in the Race to Turin following Alex de Minaur’s run to the Vienna Open final.

title: Diana Shnaider and Leylah Fernandez ranking points and prize money after Pan Pacific Open final
article_text:
Diana Shnaider won her first WTA Tour title of the year after staving off a stellar comeback from Leylah Fernandez in the Pan Pacific Open final.

The final looked like a foregone conclusion when third seed Shnaider raced to a 6-4, 4-0 lead in Tokyo on Sunday, but Fernandez had other ideas.

The 24-year-old won seven of the next eight games and took the contest into a decider. The momentum seemed to be with the Canadian, who earned three break points early in the third set.

But the Russian regained her composure, held serve and pulled away to secure a 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 victory in two hours and 18 minutes; in what was her sixth WTA title of her career.

In her on-court interview, Shnaider said, “Firstly, I would like to congratulate Leylah on an amazing week, last week, some great achievements through this Asia Swing. Congrats to you, your coach, and your family back home. Keep going and for sure hope to see you more in the finals like this in the future.”

Prior to that, Fernandez thanked the tournament organisers, the fans, her coach Eric Hechtman, and congratulated Shnaider on her triumph, which saw her rise back to a career-high ranking of 11.

“First of all I would like to congratulate Diana. An amazing week, a great match. Congratulations to you and your team. Hopefully we can have many more battles like this one,” she said.

“Second, I would like to thank my coach Eric, who is here. Thank you so much for being here this week and last. We just got to keep going. I want to thank my team who are back home watching. Without your guys’ support this wouldn’t be possible so thank you for always believing in me.”

Fernandez has enjoyed a successful Asian Swing, winning the Singapore Open and finishing runner-up in Ningbo last week and Tokyo on Sunday.

The former US Open finalist started this week in 23rd in the rankings but is up four spots to 19th. If she had won the title, Fernandez would have jumped to 16th – just three spots off her career-high.

As it is, she ends this week on 2,201 points after collecting an extra 325 points whereas Shnaider pockets 500 points of her own and is up two spots from 13th. That puts her on 3,238, just under 700 points off a top 10 spot.

For her title triumph, Shnaider has earned £138,396 and Fernandez has added £85,425 to her prize money for the year. The Canada star may yet rise the rankings again as she is scheduled to play at the WTA 250 event in Hong Kong this coming week.

title: Alexander Zverev’s Vienna Open prize money and ranking points after semi-final exit
article_text:
Alexander Zverev will claim the world No 1 ranking for the first time on Monday but will not have a new title to celebrate after defeat in the semi-final of the Vienna Open.

A runner-up at this tournament twelve months ago, Zverev was the top seed at the ATP 500 event this year and was among the favourites for glory in the Austrian capital.

However, his hopes of glory were dashed in a dramatic semi-final on Saturday, with the German tasting defeat to fifth seed Alex de Minaur.

After dropping the opening set to his Australian rival, Zverev rebounded with a dominant second set, but it was de Minaur who held firm in the closing stages to seal a 6-4, 1-6, 7-6(4) triumph — booking a date with Carlos Alcaraz in Sunday’s final.

Zverev will become the 30th world No 1 in ATP Rankings history on Monday despite his defeat but, with his campaign now over, we look at the ranking points and prize money he will take home from the event.

Significant ranking points are on offer in Vienna, with the winner of Sunday’s final between de Minaur and Alcaraz set to earn 500 ranking points, while the runner-up will take home 330 points.

Zverev earned 330 points for his runner-up finish twelve months, with 320 of those points dropping off the ATP Rankings at the start of this week.

For his semi-final run in Vienna this year, the German has earned 200 ranking points.

With the 400 ranking points he earned for reaching the semi-final of the Paris Masters last year set to drop on Monday, the German will actually drop from 9,750 to 9,550 points in the ATP Rankings.

However, with current world No 1 Jannik Sinner dropping 1,000 points from Paris and falling to 9,450 points on Monday, the 200 points gained by Zverev in Vienna this week are enough to seal his debut as the world No 1.

The German has the chance to move further ahead of Sinner next week and across the remainder of the season, with the Italian not in action for the rest of the year due to a knee injury.

Significant prize money is on offer at the ATP 500 this week, with a total prize money pool of €2,797,985 on offer across the singles and doubles events in the Austrian capital.

For reaching the semi-final of the singles events, both Zverev and third seed Daniil Medvedev — who was beaten by Alcaraz in the first semi-final of the day — will both take home €150,040 in prize money from the event.

Whoever wins Sunday’s final between Alcaraz and de Minaur will take home an impressive €523,305 in winnings, with €281,540 on offer for the beaten finalist.

title: Clarke improves as Fichardt blitzes his way to the top on PGA Tour Champions
article_text:
Darren Clarke’s four-under-par round of 68 saw him make steady progress up the leaderboard in round two of the PGA Tour Champions’ Simmons Bank Championship but South African Darren Fichardt was the story of the day as he shot an 11-under 61 that catapulted him to the top.

Clarke, fresh off a runner-up finish at last wee’s Stifel Charity Classic, shot a level-par opener and was still on that number reaching the turn on day two after two birdies and two bogeys, but an impressive back nine in which he eagled the par-5 10th and then added further bridies on the 12th and 14th saw him climb up and end the day in a tie for 28th at -4.

Pádraig Harrington’s frustrating play since returning to PGA Tour Champions action continued on day two. He began the day tied with Clarke at level-par, and also remained so through his opening nine holes. A run of four consecutive bogeys saw him plummet down the leaderboard, but he immediately bounced back to birdie the next three, then, after his only par of the back nine on 17, he closed out with an eagle-three on the last to claw his way into red figures at -1 but fall eight places on the leaderboard to T46.

With the leading 36 players on the Schwab Cup rankings qualifying for the season-ending Charles Schwab Championship in a fortnight’s time, South African Fichardt was on the outside looking in at a ranking of 46th coming into this week.

He opened with a three-under 69, but an incredible front nine in which he made an eagle and six birdies to shoot an eight-under 28 saw him storm into the mix. Three further birdies on the back nine got him into the clubhouse at 14-under-par, one shot ahead of first-round leader Zach Johnson who followed his 64 with a five-under 67.

Steven Alker and Henrik Stenson share third at -11, two behind Johnson, with the Swede also projected to climb from outside the bubble and qualify for his first Charles Schwab Championship.

Michael Block is one of four players tied for fifth, and he too is projected to climb to 35th and book his place in the season-ending championship in his rookie Champions Tour campaign.
